articles.title: MIDJOURNEY ADDS LIVE STYLE PREVIEWS AND MORE REVERSIBLE CONTROLS
articles.summary: Midjourney added live style previews in the Styles sidebar, saved prompt defaults, and undo for project deletion. Experimental previews rely on fast models and prompt text alone, and picking a style submits the prompt with it. Midjourney says its updated edit model preserves pixels outside the selected area, a claim shown only in an official demonstration, not an independent test.

articles.title: FIGMA INVESTS IN THE UK WITH EXPANDED LONDON OFFICE
articles.summary: Figma has expanded its London office at Elder Yard on Norton Folgate, deepening investment in one of its largest markets outside the United States. Two thirds of the FTSE 100 build with Figma as of Q2 2026, and over 15 million files were created in the UK in the past year. Figma's global AI report found 41% of product builders say AI meaningfully changes team collaboration, and 52% of UK respondents now say design matters more.

articles.title: APPLE'S HOMEPAD SMART HOME HUB LAUNCHING ON OCT 13 WITH IMAC G4 DESIGN
articles.summary: Apple's long-awaited HomePad smart home hub is reportedly launching October 13 with a 6-inch display and a design inspired by the iconic iMac G4. The device is expected to combine a speaker and smart home control panel with a new operating system drawing on iOS, tvOS, and watchOS, centered around Siri AI. Two versions have reportedly been developed: a tabletop model and another designed to mount on a wall.

articles.title: THE BOX DESIGN SYSTEM: AI‑READY FIGMA FILES FOR ENTERPRISE SOFTWARE
articles.summary: Flexy Global's Box Design System organizes complex enterprise product behavior into bounded Figma sections, making design files easier for people to navigate and for AI coding agents to use. Boxes form a feature, flow, and screen-state hierarchy built around behavior rather than pages, with self-contained context and arrows showing transitions. They cannot fix an undefined product or replace the design system and codebase, but as design files become inputs to AI-assisted development, this structure is becoming part of the product.

articles.title: HOW AI AGENTS ARE RESHAPING UX
articles.summary: Decagon CEO Jesse Zhang says personal AI agents such as Meta's Muse will reshape customer experience, since agents skip product displays and purchase-inducing flows. Amazon blocked Muse while Shopify opened a dedicated payment channel, though Zhang expects Amazon to back down because customers want AI assistant integration. Companies need to verify agent authority, set negotiation limits, handle exceptions, and stop fraud running at machine speed, with AI systems ultimately transacting machine to machine.

articles.title: WHAT DOES AI-READINESS MEAN IN DESIGN SYSTEMS?
articles.summary: AI-ready design systems depend less on specialized agent tooling and more on strong engineering fundamentals that make components, APIs, tokens, and documentation easy for machines to discover and understand. Testing with the Open Design System Bench found that clean separation of concerns and a single source of truth can outperform additional instruction files, which may actually hurt results when they contain stale or duplicated information. Mechanical correctness is only half the challenge: design systems also need principles and guidance that help AI exercise good design judgment rather than simply generate technically valid interfaces.

articles.title: THE SHOOT PRODUCTION PLATFORM FOR CREATIVE TEAMS
articles.summary: Run every brand shoot with confidence. From moodboards and shot lists to call sheets and shoot day, walk onto set knowing nothing was missed.

articles.title: A SEMANTIC SEARCH ENGINE FOR ARTWORKS FROM THE WORLD'S GREAT MUSEUMS
articles.summary: The Last Museum is a semantic search engine for 6.3 million artworks from the world's great museums.

articles.title: AMAZING-GLASS
articles.summary: Amazing Glass provides framework-independent web components that recreate Apple-style Liquid Glass using physically inspired refraction, interactive controls, and pixel-level comparisons against Apple's SwiftUI renderer rather than relying on simple backdrop blur.

articles.title: A SHORT UPDATE ON DESIGNING FOR FOLDABLE DEVICES
articles.summary: Three years after the Google Pixel Fold, the iPhone Duo announcement brings a fresh look at designing for foldable devices. CSS media features, a Viewport Segments API, and a Device Posture API work only in Chromium browsers, with no sign yet of Safari support. Websites needn't adapt to two screens. A dual-screen design makes sense when an experience has two simultaneous contexts, such as an inbox beside an open message.

articles.title: DO PRODUCT DESIGNERS NEED UI/UX SKILLS?
articles.summary: Product designers do need UI/UX skills, because product design spans research, wireframes, prototypes, testing, and developer collaboration, and UI/UX principles apply at nearly every stage. UI covers what users see, while UX covers whether the product works, and a beautiful app nobody can figure out still fails. Designers need not master every corner, but skills in research, wireframing, prototyping, and usability testing help them read user behavior accurately and keep decisions grounded.

articles.title: THIS PACKAGING FOR READY-MADE DINNERS CAN TEACH YOU TO COOK BETTER
articles.summary: Center's identity for chef Daniel Humm's Riff turns ready-to-cook meal packaging into a lightweight cooking lesson, showing optional fresh ingredients alongside explanations of how each changes a dish's flavor. The visual system combines a chunky curved wordmark, 12 food-inspired colors, three contrasting typefaces, deliberately unstyled food photography, and a playful mascot called Dan the Pan. Packaging reinforces the idea of improvisation with cooking tips, recipe variations, and QR codes linking to Humm's cooking videos, positioning convenience food as a starting point for learning rather than a finished product.

articles.title: GENIUS 'TILTED' APPLE WATCH BAND MAKES THE ENTIRE EXPERIENCE 10X MORE ERGONOMIC
articles.summary: A Tilted Watch Band angles the Apple Watch 30 degrees so the screen faces the wearer without a horizontal wrist, easing strain on the wrist and neck.

articles.title: MOMA EXPLORES THE USEFUL BEAUTY OF INFORMATION DESIGN
articles.summary: MoMA's exhibit Full Disclosure: The Edge of Information Design, which opened September 27, is the museum's first devoted entirely to information design.
